newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak VSZ posts SKK 1.348 bln 1996 net.
newsitem.headline: Slovak VSZ posts SKK 1.348 bln 1996 net.

text.p: Slovakia's largest steel maker VSZ a.s. said on Monday it had posted a 1.348 billion crown net profit in 1996, a nine percent increase from 1.241 billion in the previous year.
VSZ president Jan Smerek said management had proposed a 1996 dividend of 40 crowns per share after 30 crowns per share in 1995.
The results are unconsolidated, according to Slovak accounting standards and subject to an international accounting standard audit.
Company managers told a news conference at VSZ's headquarters in Kosice, eastern Slovakia, that the 1996 profit was based on total revenues of 52.07 billion crowns.
"We saw a negative trend in revenues at the end of last year, but we were able quickly to adapt to this trend, to post satisfactory results for the full year," Smerek said.
Last year, VSZ exported 85 percent of its overall production, mainly steel products.
Smerek said that 658 million crowns from last year's profit will be allocated for dividend payment, while 602 million crowns will go to the funds for further development of the plant.
"The development with our dividend, which rose by 100 percent from 1994, shows that our shares are a very lucrative security on the capital market," Smerek added.
